High catalyst run showed M2 and M13 as best fits (both involve catalyst dimerization). This suggests catalyst dimerization plays a role. M13 (irreversible dimerization to inactive) and M2 (reversible dimerization) are top candidates. M8 (ligand dissociation) also fits well. M4, M5, M20, M14, M16, M17 fit poorly now.

The aim of testing catalyst-order sensitivity was achieved: mechanisms involving cat-cat interactions rise to top.

<hypothesis>
Key discriminating features among top candidates:
- **M2 (reversible cat dimerization)**: at low [cat], no dimerization, kinetics reduce to simple M1. Rate scales linearly with [cat] at low [cat], sub-linearly at high [cat].
- **M13 (irreversible cat→cat2 sequestration)**: even at low [cat], some catalyst gets sequestered over time → reaction may stall. Rate order in [cat] similar issue but time-dependent deactivation.
- **M8 (cat ⇌ cat* + L)**: active species is cat*; behavior depends on ligand pool. Rate scaling in [cat] is fractional (typically 0.5 order).
- **M19 (cat + catS → inactive)**: bimolecular deactivation. Stalls at high catalyst.

Best discriminator: **Run at LOW catalyst concentration** with same substrate. 
- M2: reversible dimerization negligible → fits like M1, reaches completion, rate = k×[cat]×[S]
- M13: irreversible sequestration less severe at low [cat] (rate of 2cat→cat2 is second order in cat), reaction cleanly completes with rate linear in cat
- M8: fractional order — rate does not scale linearly with [cat]
- M19: minimal deactivation at low cat, reaches completion easily

Actually to distinguish M2 vs M13 specifically: run a **long-time experiment** at moderate/high cat. M2 is reversible so eventually reaches full conversion. M13 loses catalyst irreversibly, could show stalling.

Even better test: high catalyst with LOW substrate. This lets us observe catalyst behavior more clearly:
- M13: irreversible loss → final conversion < 100% if catalyst dies before substrate is consumed
- M2: reversible → full conversion still
- M8: fractional order still

Let me try [cat]=0.1, [S]=0.3 — with limited substrate the reaction should complete quickly. If it stalls, M13 confirmed.

Actually, more informative: [cat]=0.005 (very low), [S]=1.0. 
- M2: rate linear in cat, ~50× slower than run_2 but complete
- M13: rate linear in cat (initial), reaches completion (dimerization negligible)
- M8: rate ~sqrt(cat/L), gives different scaling; may plateau if ligand is limiting
- M19: no deactivation, clean

Compare initial rate ratios to distinguish M8 from M2/M13. Also test at very low cat to see if M2 differs from M13 (M13 would still show some loss; M2 collapses to M1 behavior).
</hypothesis>
